In 20Co alloy deformed at 10 s−1, apart from the well-developed DTs and DCs in γ channel, SFs in the same {111} plane are prevalent within the γp′ precipitates (Fig. 3a).
In 20Co alloy deformed at 10 s−1, apart from the well-developed DTs and DCs in γ channel

SFs in the same {111} plane are prevalent within the γp′ precipitates (Fig. 3a). These SFs nucleated at one side of the γp′ interface, propagated forward to the other side. High resolution TEM observation demonstrates that the intrinsic nature of these SFs is superlattice extrinsic SFs (Fig. 3b).

When the strain rate was reduced to 10−2 s−1, the formation of NGs are greatly enhanced, NGs distribute all over the observed region, rather than only restricted to the shear band zone as 13Co alloy ( Fig. 3 c). The magniﬁed image in Fig. 3 d showed the polygonal shape of NGs, revealing their mature feature as aN G .

An original subgrain containing several nano-sized blocks is shown in Fig. 4a, in which four blocks with small misorientation (named as a–d) and two blocks with high misorientation (named as e, f) can be clearly distinguished.
Further observation reveals that these blocks can be produced by the intersection and encirclement of SFs and MTs ( Fig. 4b).

mechanisms.name: deformation twinning via diffusion-controlled reordering of overlapping complex stacking faults

evidence.quote: Pseudo twins will form after the overlapping of four consecutive complex SF (CSF) on {111} planes and transform into a true MT after the atom reordering. This process is thermally activated that needs high temperature (650–800 °C) and low strain rate to ensure sufﬁcient energy and time for atoms to diffusion

mechanisms.name: dislocation cross-slip hindrance by decreased stacking fault energy

evidence.quote: decreasing the SFE of two superalloys by adding Co element can hinder the cross-slip of dislocations, promote the decorrelation of a/2 〈110〉 matrix dislocations into Shockley partials, and facilitate the initiation of SFs and MTs in the matrix
The dynamic introduction of NGs during compressive deformation probably acts as strong obstacles for dislocation motion, resulting in dispersion strengthening in materials.

It can be inferred that the formation of NG depends on whether MT exist in deformed microstructure, meanwhile the proportion of NGs is also correlated to the content of MT in two alloys.

It is revealed that compressive stress at relatively low strain rate can be enhanced apparently through decreasing the SFE, introducing certain quantity of NGs to produce dynamic dispersion strengthening in the Ni-Co based superalloys.
